name_note: GTDB places this species in the genus Clostridium_AQ; its genomes are named [Clostridium] innocuum in NCBI and the organism is called Clostridium innocuum in the literature.

sentences.text: Clostridium innocuum is an anaerobic gram-positive spore-forming bacterium and a commensal member of the human gut microbiome.

A case report with systematic review described bacteraemia with this organism complicating a foot ulcer, and reviewed associations from diarrhoea and local infections to inflammatory bowel disease and kidney disease.

C. innocuum is increasingly detected in patients with Clostridioides difficile infection, particularly following vancomycin treatment, and has been reported as associated with delayed clinical recovery and poor outcomes.
In co-infection models in human intestinal epithelial cells, C. innocuum alone showed minimal cytotoxicity but enhanced cell death and barrier disruption alongside toxigenic C. difficile.
That study described the organism's intrinsic vancomycin resistance as enabling survival and expansion during treatment of C. difficile infection.
